question: I'm a University of Luxembourg student who has been nominated for an Erasmus exchange next semester. What administrative steps should I complete before departure, and what should I check regarding my Learning Agreement, language requirements, accommodation and travel documents?
expected_key_points: Wait for the Outgoing Mobility Office email before starting the host university application.
Respect the host university application deadlines.
Complete a Learning Agreement of at least 30 ECTS and obtain the required signatures.
Complete the OLS language evaluation if the teaching language is not the student's mother tongue.
Complete the required enrolment steps and upload the signed mobility contract through the mobility portal.
Arrange accommodation and check health insurance, passport validity and visa requirements.
answer:
Based on the official sources, here are the administrative steps and checks you need to complete before your Erasmus exchange:

Administrative Steps Before Departure

1. Host Institution Application: Wait for an email from the Outgoing Mobility Office containing instructions for your host university application. Winter semester instructions are sent between April and June, while summer semester instructions are sent between late August and November. Do not start your application before receiving this email. You must submit your application to the host university by its own deadlines and arrange your own housing (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/, Last checked: 12.11.2026).

2. Learning Agreement (LA) or Online Learning Agreement (OLA): Complete a learning agreement, which is mandatory to validate your mobility. First, check whether your host institution uses a PDF/Word learning agreement or the OLA (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/, Last checked: 12.11.2026). If you are an FDEF student creating an OLA via learning-agreement.eu, you must log in using MyAcademicID with your student ID, select the correct ISCED field of education, list your courses in Table A for at least 30 ECTS (for Bachelor students), and enter Mobility window in Table B before signing and submitting it for review by your faculty mobility specialist and host institution (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/02/FDEF-How-to-create-and-fill-out-my-Online-Learning-Agreement-OLA-FDEST.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026).

3. Erasmus+ Language Evaluation: If the teaching language is not your mother tongue, you must take a mandatory language evaluation via Online Linguistic Support (OLS). Results below B2 will lead to online language courses (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/, Last checked: 12.11.2026).

4. Erasmus+ Grant and Mobility Contract: Eligible students receive the Erasmus+ grant automatically without applying. Before leaving, you must sign the Grant Agreement (mobility contract) and upload your signed contract through the mobility portal (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/, Last checked: 12.11.2026 and https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026). Also, make sure to check that your bank details are up to date in the Guichet Etudiant before the grant payment is processed (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026).

5. Re-enrolment: Enrol as an outgoing international exchange student at the University of Luxembourg and as an incoming student at your host university. You only pay enrolment fees at the University of Luxembourg, though German universities Semesterbeitrag fees cannot be waived (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/, Last checked: 12.11.2026).

Learning Agreement Requirements to Check

- The learning agreement must cover at least 30 ECTS and must be signed by you, your programme director (via your faculty mobility contact), and your host institution (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- If you are following the FDEF specific guidelines, you cannot choose courses you have already taken or will take upon your return to Unilux, and courses must match your field of study. You may choose one language course provided it is not in your native language, not French or German (if you went through the Luxembourgish school system), and not at a level higher than B2 (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/02/FDEF-How-to-create-and-fill-out-my-Online-Learning-Agreement-OLA-FDEF.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026).

Language Requirements

- If the language of instruction is not your mother tongue, you must complete the Erasmus+ language evaluation (Online Linguistic Support / OLS). Scoring below B2 will result in assigned online language courses (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/, Last checked: 12.11.2026). Note that this evaluation is generally not accepted as an official language test like TOEFL or IELTS (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/, Last checked: 12.11.2026).

Accommodation

- Finding accommodation is your own responsibility. Because rooms are limited, you should apply early. You should also beware of housing scams and consider reaching out to the local ESN association for assistance (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/, Last checked: 12.11.2026).

Travel Documents and Insurance

- Check your passport validity and visa requirements, as some partner institutions require validity that extends beyond your mobility period (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Secure adequate health insurance. You can also utilize International SOS, which offers free 24/7 assistance for mobility trips (though it is an assistance provider, not an insurance company) (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- If applicable, look into the Green Travel top-up, which covers travel between your main residence and the host university and back, and requires a Declaration of Honour Green Travel (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/, Last checked: 12.11.2026).

Recommendation: Since the International Relations Office (BRI) is responsible for coordinating Erasmus+ student mobility, you should contact the BRI if you need any further clarification or have questions regarding your mobility process (Recommendation based on documented responsibilities).

question: I'm preparing for my Erasmus exchange and need to organise my paperwork. Which documents and administrative forms do I need to complete, who needs to sign them, and what must I upload through the University's mobility portal?
expected_key_points: Prepare a Learning Agreement (LA or OLA) covering at least 30 ECTS.
Obtain the required signatures from the student, programme director and host institution.
Upload the signed mobility contract through the mobility portal.
Complete the OLS language evaluation if the teaching language is not the student's mother tongue.
answer:
Based on the official sources, here are the documents, administrative forms, required signatures, and items you must upload for your Erasmus exchange:

Documents and administrative forms to complete:
- Certificate of arrival: Must be completed, signed, and stamped by the host university https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Learning Agreement (or Online Learning Agreement - OLA): Must cover at least 30 ECTS (for Bachelor students) and be signed by you, your programme director (through your faculty's mobility contact), and your host institution https://eu1.hubs.ly/H/0t48mB50; https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/ (Last checked: 12.11.2026). If your host university does not use OLA, you complete the "during the mobility" form (Word format), sign it, and have it validated by your host university https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026). If there are course changes within the month of arrival, you must update your learning agreement using the OLA instructions or the Word form modifications https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Certificate of end of stay: Must be completed, signed, and stamped by the host university https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Online mobility report: Completed online after receiving the invitation in your Unilu student inbox https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Grant Agreement (Mobility Contract): Must be signed by you and the Vice-Rector before departure or during your first month of mobility https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/FAQ-Erasmus-FR_DE_-EN_24-25.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Top-up documents (if applicable): If requesting a "fewer opportunities" top-up, you may need a doctor-completed form provided by the University, a household composition certificate, proof that children spent the mobility period abroad, or a residence permit indicating refugee status https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Green Travel documents (if applicable): A Declaration of Honour Green Travel is referenced for the Green Travel top-up https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/ (Last checked: 12.11.2026).

Signatures required:
- Certificate of arrival and certificate of end of stay: Signed and stamped by the host university https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Learning Agreement (OLA or Word form): Signed by you, your programme director (via faculty mobility contact), and your host institution https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/; https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/02/FDEF-How-to-create-and-fill-out-my-Online-Learning-Agreement-OLA-FDEF.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Grant Agreement (Mobility contract): Signed by you and the Vice-Rector https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/FAQ-Erasmus-FR_DE_-EN_24-25.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).

What must be uploaded through the University's mobility portal:
- A PDF copy of the certificate of arrival https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Your signed mobility contract https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/; https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/FAQ-Erasmus-FR_DE_-EN_24-25.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- A PDF copy of the certificate of end of stay upon leaving https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- A PDF copy of your learning agreement and of any modifications signed by all parties upon leaving https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).

*(Note: While the sources detail what documents to upload to the mobility portal, they do not explicitly list every single portal upload step for optional items like top-up forms, which are handled via email instructions.)*

If you need clarification regarding Erasmus+ or student mobility, a reasonable recommendation based on its documented responsibilities is to contact the International Relations Office (BRI Outgoing via bri.outgoing@uni.lu), as it coordinates Erasmus+ student mobility and manages related documentation and grants.

question: I'm choosing courses at my host university and want to make sure they will count towards my degree at the University of Luxembourg. What needs to be agreed upon in my Learning Agreement, what happens if I change courses during my exchange, and how are the credits recognised when I return?
expected_key_points: Agree on the courses and their recognition through the Learning Agreement.
Use the Learning Agreement to record the courses and ECTS.
If courses change during mobility, update the Learning Agreement using Table A2.
Provide reasons for exceptional course changes.
Obtain the required signatures from the student, host institution and sending institution.
Credits agreed in the Learning Agreement and confirmed by the Transcript of Records are automatically recognised according to the form.
answer:
What needs to be agreed upon in your Learning Agreement:
You must complete a Learning Agreement (academic contract) detailing your choice of courses at the host institution, which must be approved by both responsible coordinators at your home and host institutions https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/02/FDEF-How-to-create-and-fill-out-my-Online-Learning-Agreement-OLA-FDEF.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026). By signing the agreement, they agree to you taking the courses and your home university validating them upon your return if successfully completed https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/02/FDEF-How-to-create-and-fill-out-my-Online-Learning-Agreement-OLA-FDEF.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026). For Bachelor students, you need to choose courses for at least 30 ECTS in total (Master students are also advised to choose 30 ECTS) https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/02/FDEF-How-to-create-and-fill-out-my-Online-Learning-Agreement-OLA-FDEF.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026). In Table B (recognition at the sending institution), you must enter "Mobility window" in the fields Component Title and Component Code, "30" in Number of ECTS credits, and select your semester of departure https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/02/FDEF-How-to-create-and-fill-out-my-Online-Learning-Agreement-OLA-FDEF.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026). 

What happens if you change courses during your exchange:
If you need to make changes before or during the first month of your stay, you can update your learning agreement https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/02/FDEF-How-to-create-and-fill-out-my-Online-Learning-Agreement-OLA-FDEF.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026), https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026). If using the Online Learning Agreement (OLA), you log in, select Apply changes, add or delete components in Table A2 while completing the "reason change" field, and submit it for approval by both coordinators https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/02/FDEF-How-to-create-and-fill-out-my-Online-Learning-Agreement-OLA-FDEF.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026). Table B should never be changed https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/02/FDEF-How-to-create-and-fill-out-my-Online-Learning-Agreement-OLA-FDEF.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026). If your host university does not use OLA, you must complete the Word form for changes during the mobility (Table A2 and Table C2 for virtual components), sign it, have it validated by the host university, and send it back for validation by the sending institution https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/Modification_Learning_Agreement_Erasmus_outgoing_students.docx (Last checked: 12.11.2026), https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026). You must get approval from both universities before making your final course choices to avoid risking non-validation https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/02/FDEF-How-to-create-and-fill-out-my-Online-Learning-Agreement-OLA-FDEF.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).

How credits are recognised when you return:
Upon returning from mobility, you must provide your original Transcript of Records from the host university to your academic contact to validate your ECTS https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026). An electronic version is only accepted if sent directly by the host university to the academic contact; otherwise, it must be a certified and protected copy https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026), https://www.uni.lu/fdef-en/study-abroad/ (Last checked: 12.11.2026). The latest and approved version of your Learning Agreement must correspond with the Transcript of Records, and only credits from courses approved on the final Learning Agreement are validated https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/02/FDEF-How-to-create-and-fill-out-my-Online-Learning-Agreement-OLA-FDEF.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026), https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/free-mover/ (Last checked: 14.11.2026). The programme director recognises the ECTS earned abroad based on this signed learning agreement https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/ (Last checked: 12.11.2026).

If you have questions or need clarification regarding Erasmus+ or student mobility, it is recommended to contact the International Relations Office (BRI), as they are responsible for coordinating Erasmus+ student mobility.

question: I've completed my Erasmus nomination and submitted my application to the host university, but I still haven't received an acceptance letter. What does the University of Luxembourg's official guidance say I should do, and who should I contact if the procedure isn't specified?
expected_key_points: Clearly acknowledge that the available sources do not specify what to do when an acceptance letter has not arrived.
Suggest contacting the relevant mobility office for clarification, while making clear this is a recommendation rather than a documented procedure.
Do not invent a deadline, alternative document or acceptance-letter procedure.
answer:
The supplied official sources do not contain specific guidance on what to do if you have submitted your application to the host university but have not yet received an acceptance letter. 

As a recommended next step, based on the documented responsibilities described in the official sources, if you need clarification about Erasmus+ or student mobility, you should contact the International Relations Office (BRI) at bri.outgoing@uni.lu https://www.uni.lu/fdef-en/study-abroad/ (Last checked: 12.11.2026).

question: I'm preparing for an Erasmus semester in another European country. What health insurance arrangements should I make before leaving, and what is the difference between the European Health Insurance Card and the International SOS assistance service?
expected_key_points: Arrange adequate health insurance before travelling.
Know that International SOS provides free 24/7 assistance for mobility trips.
Ensure that the European Health Insurance Card is valid for the entire mobility period.
Understand that International SOS is not an insurance provider and does not replace health insurance.
Distinguish between health insurance coverage and the assistance service provided by International SOS.
answer:
Before leaving for your Erasmus semester, you should check whether your European health insurance card is valid for the whole mobility period https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026). You also need to get adequate health insurance https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/ (Last checked: 12.11.2026). Additionally, you should download the International SOS assistance app and follow the instructions received via email https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).

Regarding the difference between the two services:
- The European Health Insurance Card serves as your health insurance coverage for your stay https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- The International SOS assistance service provides free 24/7 assistance for mobility trips, but it is explicitly noted that it is not a health insurance provider or a health insurance itself https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026), https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/ (Last checked: 12.11.2026).

question: I've been accepted at a host university but haven't arranged accommodation yet. What should I consider when looking for housing, including availability, location, costs and the responsibilities I have as an exchange student?
expected_key_points: Consider accommodation costs when comparing the cost of living at the destination.
Check the location of the host university campus because courses may take place away from the main study location.
Consider accommodation availability and location when preparing for the exchange.
Understand that accommodation is the student's responsibility and that applying early is recommended.
answer:
When looking for housing as an exchange student, you should consider the following:

Responsibilities and general considerations:
- Accommodation is your own responsibility. Rooms are limited, so you should apply early (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/, Last checked: 12.11.2026; https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/free-mover/, Last checked: 14.11.2026; https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/11/GEP_Presentation.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- You should beware of housing scams, and you can consider contacting the local ESN association for help (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- The host institution's website may also help you find accommodation (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/free-mover/, Last checked: 14.11.2026).

Costs and Location:
- Living costs, including accommodation, vary by country and city, with Northern European countries generally being more expensive than Southern ones (https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=10573, Last checked: 14.11.2026).
- You should also check the campus location of your courses, as they may be held on campuses far from the main study location, which may impact your housing location choice (https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=10573, Last checked: 14.11.2026).

Regarding your next steps and clarification, since the International Relations Office (BRI) is responsible for coordinating Erasmus+ student mobility, it is recommended to contact the BRI if you need further guidance or assistance with your mobility preparations.

question: I'm planning an Erasmus exchange and want to build a realistic budget. How should I estimate my living expenses based on the destination's cost of living, calculate the financial support I may receive through the monthly Erasmus grant, travel contribution and fewer-opportunities top-up, and account for the minimum and maximum funded mobility durations and the timing of grant payments? Also, what potential expenses are not covered by the University's financial guidance?
expected_key_points: Estimate living expenses such as accommodation, food and leisure.
Consider differences in the cost of living between destinations.
Check the Erasmus monthly grant applicable to the destination.
Consider the travel contribution, which depends on the distance band.
Check whether eligible students can receive the fewer-opportunities top-up.
Account for the minimum and maximum funded mobility durations.
Plan for upfront expenses because 70% of the grant is paid at the beginning and the remaining amount is recalculated after mobility.
Clearly identify expenses for which the available financial guidance provides no specific information, rather than inventing costs or assuming the grant covers everything.
answer:
Based on the official sources, here is how you can estimate and calculate your financial support and budget for an Erasmus exchange:

Estimating Living Expenses Based on Cost of Living
When choosing a receiving institution, you should note that living costs for food, accommodation, and leisure vary by country and city, and northern European countries are generally more expensive than southern ones https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=10573 (Last checked: 14.11.2026). Furthermore, accommodation is your responsibility, meaning you must arrange your own housing https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/ (Last checked: 12.11.2026).

Monthly Erasmus Grant by Country Group
Eligible students receive an Erasmus grant automatically without needing to apply https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/ (Last checked: 12.11.2026). The monthly contribution to living costs depends on your destination country https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026):
- Group 1 (606 EUR per month): Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Liechtenstein, Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, and third countries not associated with the programme (United Kingdom and Switzerland) https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026). Note that for Switzerland, exchanges are under the Swiss-European Mobility Programme where mobility periods are generally funded by the Swiss institution unless they do not provide funding, in which case Erasmus+ funds it subject to an inter-institutional agreement https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Group 2 (550 EUR per month): Cyprus, Czechia, Estonia, Greece, Latvia, Malta, Portugal, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Group 3 (550 EUR per month): Bulgaria, Croatia, Hungary, Lithuania, North Macedonia, Poland, Romania, Serbia, Turkey https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Local mobility under 100 km from the University of Luxembourg's registered office (such as Nancy, Metz, Longwy, Trier, Saarbrucken, Birkenfeld, Arlon, Libramont): 0 EUR https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).

Travel Contribution
You may receive a contribution to travel costs based on the distance travelled between the home institution's registered office and the place of activity abroad, as calculated by the European Commission's distance calculator https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026):
- Between 100 and 499 km: 211 EUR https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Between 500 and 1,999 km: 309 EUR https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Between 2,000 and 2,999 km: 395 EUR https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Between 3,000 and 3,999 km: 580 EUR https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Between 4,000 and 7,999 km: 1,188 EUR https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- 8,000 km or more: 1,735 EUR https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
A maximum of two additional days of travel costs may also be allocated (1 day for distances under 1,000 km, 2 days for 1,000 km or more) https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026). (Note: A Green Travel top-up is also referenced for travel between your main residence and host university, though exact monetary values for it are not detailed in that specific text section) https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/ (Last checked: 12.11.2026).

Fewer-Opportunities Top-Up
A "fewer opportunities" top-up of 250 EUR per month can be added if you qualify https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026). Eligibility applies to students with a physical or mental disability incurring additional costs, health problems/chronic or severe illness incurring additional costs, a child/children taken along for the mobility period, or refugee status https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026). Note that only students receiving a contribution to living costs are eligible for a travel allowance and this top-up https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).

Minimum and Maximum Funded Mobility Durations
- Effective duration minimum: The mobility period must last at least 60 days; if it is less, the full grant must be refunded https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026). 
- Maximum funded duration: The Erasmus grant is awarded for a maximum of 150 days for a mobility period in a programme-associated country, and a maximum of 135 days for a non-associated country https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).

Timing of Grant Payments
The Erasmus grant is paid in two instalments:
1. 70% of the maximum amount at the start of the mobility period (specifically, minimum 4 weeks after receipt of your mobility contract with your signature via the mobility portal) https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026), https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/FAQ-Erasmus-FR_DE_-EN_24-25.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
2. The remaining balance at the end of the mobility period (at least 4 weeks after receipt of compulsory end-of-stay documents via the mobility portal) https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/FAQ-Erasmus-FR_DE_-EN_24-25.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026). The exact grant amount is recalculated based on the actual start and end dates indicated on your certificates https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026), https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/FAQ-Erasmus-FR_DE_-EN_24-25.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026). If the actual duration is longer than planned, there is no additional scholarship, and if it is shorter, the total amount is reduced https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/FAQ-Erasmus-FR_DE_-EN_24-25.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).

What Expenses Are Not Covered by the Financial Guidance
The provided sources do not explicitly itemize or cover general personal living expenses (such as specific daily grocery, leisure, or utility costs), specific health insurance premiums (though health insurance is noted as a requirement to obtain, and International SOS provides free assistance rather than insurance coverage) https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/ (Last checked: 12.11.2026), passport or visa fees, or specific local fees like German universities' "Semesterbeitrag" fees (which cannot be waived) https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/ (Last checked: 12.11.2026). Furthermore, government-run grant schemes like AideFi are separate from the University's managed funding https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).

Recommendation: Since the International Relations Office (BRI) is responsible for coordinating Erasmus+ student mobility, you should contact the BRI at bri.outgoing@uni.lu if you need clarification or assistance regarding your Erasmus mobility and funding arrangements.

question: I've found conflicting or unclear instructions on an official University of Luxembourg webpage about my Erasmus mobility. Which University office is responsible for coordinating student mobility, and whom should I approach for clarification?
expected_key_points: Identify the Bureau des Relations Internationales (BRI) as the office that coordinates and promotes Erasmus+ student mobility.
Recommend contacting the BRI for clarification about international mobility, while making clear this is a recommendation based on its responsibilities.
Do not invent a contact person, contact details or response deadline.
answer:
The International Relations Office (BRI) is responsible for coordinating the Erasmus+ programme and student mobility https://www.uni.lu/en/about/organisation/administration/international-relations-office/ (Last checked: 12.11.2026). 

Based on the documented responsibilities of the International Relations Office (BRI) as the coordinator of Erasmus+ student mobility, it is recommended that you contact the BRI for clarification https://www.uni.lu/en/about/organisation/administration/international-relations-office/ (Last checked: 12.11.2026). 

Depending on your faculty and specific administrative matters, you may also reach out to the Outgoing Mobility Office (BRI) or faculty mobility contacts, such as BRIO (bri.outgoing@uni.lu) https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/ (Last checked: 12.11.2026), https://www.uni.lu/fdef-en/study-abroad/ (Last checked: 12.11.2026).

question: I'm preparing a timeline for my upcoming Erasmus semester. Which important deadlines and administrative milestones should I track before departure, after arriving at the host university, at the end of my exchange and after returning to Luxembourg?
expected_key_points: Regularly check the university student email account for mobility instructions.
Ensure the European Health Insurance Card is valid before departure.
After arrival, obtain the signed and stamped Certificate of Arrival and upload it to the mobility portal.
Update the Learning Agreement within the first month after arrival if courses or ECTS change.
At the end of the exchange, obtain and upload the Certificate of End of Stay and the required Learning Agreement documents.
Complete the online mobility report.
After returning, provide the required Transcript of Records to the academic contact.
answer:
Based on the provided official sources, here are the important administrative milestones and deadlines to track across the different stages of your Erasmus mobility:

Before departure:
- Prepare for your mobility semester one academic year before departure (https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=10573, Last checked: 14.11.2026).
- Attend the mandatory info session for Bachelor students held at Study Abroad Day, which takes place every year in November on the second Thursday (https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=10573, Last checked: 14.11.2026).
- Erasmus+ selection takes place at the beginning of the summer semester for the following full academic year; for mobility in semester 3 or 4, apply at the beginning of semester 2, and for mobility in semester 5, apply at the beginning of semester 4 (https://www.uni.lu/fdef-en/study-abroad/, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Complete your application at the receiving institution, complete your Learning Agreement (LA) or Online Learning Agreement (OLA), complete the Erasmus+ language evaluation / Online Linguistic Support (OLS), arrange your Erasmus+ grant, and handle re-enrolment at the University of Luxembourg along with signing your mobility contract (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/, Last checked: 12.11.2026). 
- Note that specific calendar-date application deadlines are not stated on the general pages; you must consult the linked application procedures or the International Relations Office (https://www.uni.lu/fdef-en/study-abroad/, Last checked: 12.11.2026).

After arriving at the host university (During your study exchange):
- Complete Step 8 by staying in touch with your faculty contact person, programme director, and the Outgoing Mobility Office, and upload your Certificate of Arrival via the mobility portal (https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=12305, Last checked: 14.11.2026).
- If needed, modify your Learning Agreement or Online Learning Agreement before or during the first month of your stay (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/02/FDEF-How-to-create-and-fill-out-my-Online-Learning-Agreement-OLA-FDEF.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026, https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=12305, Last checked: 14.11.2026). Be sure to respect any strict deadlines set by your host university for course changes and OLA submissions (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/02/FDEF-How-to-create-and-fill-out-my-Online-Learning-Agreement-OLA-FDEN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026).

At the end of your exchange (Before your return):
- Complete Step 9 after your exam period, triggered by an email sent to your student address (https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=12305, Last checked: 14.11.2026).
- Get the Certificate of Departure signed by your host university and upload it to the portal (https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=12305, Last checked: 14.11.2026).
- Ensure your Learning Agreement and any modifications are signed by both institutions and uploaded (https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=12305, Last checked: 14.11.2026).
- Complete and submit the end-of-stay report (Erasmus+ participant report), which arrives automatically on your mobility contract's end-of-stay date (https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=12305, Last checked: 14.11.2026). All departure documents and this report are mandatory to validate your mobility semester (https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=12305, Last checked: 14.11.2026).

After returning to Luxembourg (After your study exchange):
- Proceed to Step 10: ensure your host university issues and sends your Transcript of Records (TOR) to recognize your ECTS credits, keeping in mind that the transcript courses must match your final approved Learning Agreement (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/, Last checked: 12.11.2026, https://www.uni.lu/fdef-en/study-abroad/, Last checked: 12.11.2026). For FDEF students, you are responsible for obtaining the transcript and should ask the host university to send a copy to Stephanie Anderson (stephanie.anderson@uni.lu) (https://www.uni.lu/fdef-en/study-abroad/, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Share your experience as outlined in Step 10 (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/, Last checked: 12.11.2026).

If you need clarification regarding Erasmus+ or student mobility, it is recommended to contact the International Relations Office (BRI / BRIO) as they are responsible for coordinating Erasmus+ student mobility and handling administrative matters (https://aws-or-inferred-responsibility, https://www.uni.lu/fdef-en/study-abroad/, Last checked: 12.11.2026).

question: I'm already studying at my host university and have encountered academic issues, including changes to my selected courses. When should I get in touch with my home university's programme director or faculty mobility coordinator, particularly regarding course changes and credit recognition?
expected_key_points: Recognise that the programme director is responsible for recognising ECTS earned abroad.
Understand that credit recognition is based on the Learning Agreement signed before the exchange.
Recommend contacting the programme director or relevant faculty mobility contact about academic recognition or agreed courses, while identifying this as a recommendation.
answer:
You should get in touch regarding course changes before or during the first month of your stay at the host university, ensuring you obtain approval from both your home and host universities before making your final course choice https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/02/FDEF-How-to-create-and-fill-out-my-Online-Learning-Agreement-OLA-FDEF.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026). If you encounter academic issues such as unavailable courses, schedule overlaps, or a change of mind requiring modifications to your Learning Agreement, you must send the modified Learning Agreement as soon as possible and before the host university's modification deadline https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/free-mover/ (Last checked: 14.11.2026). 

Regarding credit recognition and validation, a fully signed final Learning Agreement is required by the end of your mobility to validate successfully completed courses https://www.uni.lu/fdef-en/study-abroad/ (Last checked: 12.11.2026). If you face failed exams and re-sits are not possible, you should consult the Dettes de mobilite section in your study programme's Moodle documentation or contact your study programme administrator https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/free-mover/ (Last checked: 14.11.2026).

The provided sources do not specify any other exact timelines or calendar dates for contacting your home university regarding these issues beyond the first month of your stay. As a recommendation based on documented responsibilities, if you need clarification or guidance during your mobility, you may contact the International Relations Office (BRI) or your faculty mobility contact (such as Stephanie Anderson for FDEF) https://www.uni.lu/fdef-en/study-abroad/ (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
